title: How To Stop Worrying And Start Living

questions.q: What three steps does Carnegie recommend for clearing confusion?
a: Get the facts, analyze them, then decide
Rest, exercise, then revisit the problem
Talk it out, forget it, then move on
Write a list, delegate it, then review it
questions.why: Lesson 1 lays out gathering facts, analyzing options and committing to a decision.

questions.q: In the Galen Litchfield story, which option did he choose?
a: Act as if nothing had happened
Flee the country immediately
Explain himself to the admiral
Hide the valuable items
questions.why: Lesson 1 says Litchfield decided to carry on normally, and the feared punishment never came.

questions.q: What is a stop-loss in the summary's advice?
a: A preset limit that caps how much you will lose
A list of every possible thing that could go wrong
A rule for avoiding all financial risk
A timer for making decisions quickly
questions.why: Lesson 2 borrows the trading term to mean setting a firm boundary on worry and grief.

questions.q: What does the summary suggest doing with criticism?
a: See it as proof you are on track
Argue back until the critic concedes
Ignore all feedback completely
Collect it and review it once a year
questions.why: Lesson 3 says most critics are envious, so criticism can indicate you are doing something right.

questions.q: Why does the summary say people criticize others?
a: They feel threatened by your success
They want to help improve your work
They are paid to evaluate performance
They enjoy debating small topics
questions.why: Lesson 3 says people offer opinions to feel better about themselves when they envy you.
